audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check passes: every span of the deciding quote, the domain quote and the exceptions quote is in the held vdT 1864 djvu text at the stated places (Mandailingsch klankstelsel H p.31 = line 2392; Toba par.18-20 + Aanm.1-2 = lines 1707-1855), verbatim modulo scanned. (2) The classification rests on a 19th-century reference grammar whose Mandailing section defers to the Toba chapter; that chapter describes a right-edge penult/final contrast governed by word class, syntactic function, suffixation and, for 'many words', lexical arbitrariness with minimal pairs -- lexical with a set by morphology secondary is a faithful reading. sources.quote: p.147-148: 'Tekanan pada kata yang bersuku dua dalam bahasa Batak Angkola dapat dibedakan atas dua jenis, yaitu (1) nomina dan verba mendapat tekanan yang lebih keras pada suku pertama ... /i-gung/ hidung, /ba-gas/ rumah, /ma-nuk/ ayam, /ma-ngan/ makan, /mo-dom/ tidur; (2) adjektiva dan kata tambahan mendapat tekanan yang lebih keras pada suku kedua: /je-ges/ cantik, /jor-but/ jelek, /ba-gas/ dalam, /si-gop/ cepat, /lam-bat/ lambat ... nomina dan verba mempunyai tekanan (1-3), sedangkan adjektiva dan kata tambahan mempunyai tekanan (3-1).' p.148-149: three-syllable words strongest stress on th
sources.locator: sec. 3.2.1 Tekanan, pp.147-149 (the text layer); summary sec. 4 items f-g, p.157 (the text layer); p.17 (the text layer) on phonemic stress in Toba bontar/bagas
sources.note: Only modern phonology of the Angkola-Mandailing cluster with an explicit stress section (pp.147-149); our Mandailing coding rests on an 1864 one-line cross-reference to the Toba chapter. downloaded now; confirms word-class-conditioned penult/final contrast (bagas 'house' vs bagas 'inside') and penult in longer words.

sources.note: Describes Batak Angkola (ISO akb, Tapanuli Selatan), a distinct Glottolog languoid and the closest sister variety of Mandailing (btm); the book's own cataloguing heading is 'Bahasa Batak Angkola-Mandailing-Fonologi' and the 2016 regional dictionary treats Angkola-Mandailing as one lexicon. The catalog record for Mandailingsch has an empty rule and no existing statements, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict; this is the best available proxy statement and should be recorded as Angkola-based, not as a Mandailing-proper source. scanned artefacts in the ('umurnnya', 'ernpat', 'dalarn'…
